evidence: The mechanism is mechanically possible but is neither new nor a defect by this codebase's own design. process_inbox_pr_review reads the enabled config with a plain writer-pinned SELECT and no lock (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1149), fetches the PR from GitHub (tasks.py:1154-1161; one GET, 15s request timeout at products/stamphog/backend/logic/github_client.py:423), then opens the run-creation transaction, which locks only ReviewRun rows and never reloads or re-checks the config (tasks.py:1185-1231). The disable path is two autocommit statements with no lock: perform_update/perform_destroy save enabled=False, then _supersede_active_runs bulk-updates non-terminal runs (products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:225-253); the installation-removal path has the same shape (tasks.py:703-717, 785-792). The workflow never re-reads enabled: post_verdict guards only on SUPERSEDED status and head movement (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:650-713) and no activity touches StamphogRepoConfig.enabled (grep of temporal/ finds only digest_enabled at activities.py:1158); views.py:242-245 states this explicitly as the reason the disable path supersedes instead. So a disable committed between tasks.py:1149 and the commit at 1231 does yield one run the disable misses. Why it is not real: (1) it duplicates the pre-existing webhook path exactly. process_pull_request_event gates on repo_config.enabled at tasks.py:925 after an unlocked _resolve_repo_config (tasks.py:289-304), then makes a GitHub call for uncached authors (_author_lacks_write_permission, tasks.py:237-257, 966-969), two more reads (tasks.py:988-1023), and only then the transaction at tasks.py:1035-1066 with no config re-check; the inbox leg's docstring says it mirrors that sequence (tasks.py:1121-1123), and master still has no config re-check in either leg. (2) The window is one GitHub GET plus a few DB round trips, typically sub-second and capped by the 15s timeout; every Celery retry re-enters at the config SELECT (tasks.py:1152-1161, 1232-1234) and every receiver refire re-runs the enabled=True filter (tasks.py:1126-1128, 1140-1149), so queue latency and refires do not widen it. (3) The consequence is the stale-approval class the design already tolerates and cleans up: perform_destroy's comment (views.py:226-230) and the disabled-repo skip at tasks.py:925-936 (test_tasks.py:246-254) retract a disabled repo's standing approval on the next head change, and the inbox leg only reviews bot-authored drafts whose acting reviewer opted in (tasks.py:1112-1119). No privilege escalation, no data loss, no path an attacker controls; a user must click disable inside a sub-second window to see one verdict they can dismiss. The suggested lock-and-reload is defensive hardening that would apply equally to the webhook leg.
notes: I would upgrade to consider/should_fix if the webhook leg or the disable path were shown to lock or re-check the config inside the creation transaction (making the inbox leg the only unguarded path), if a stale approval minted after disable were not retracted on the next head change, or if the config read sat before a queue hop or the GitHub fetch could stall for minutes rather than the 15s timeout. It would be must_fix only if the run-time verdict could grant something the repo owner did not previously authorize, which it cannot: the config was enabled when the run was gated.
